snapshot_note: v0.51.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 — forest-carriers S6, madc.ini: THE CARRIERS TRACK IS DONE. madc optionally reads one madc.ini and settings resolve CLI > environment > madc.ini > baked defaults — the rule the S3 chain reserved its last arm for. Keys: std / forest (discovery ARM 5, the last arm) / include (repeatable, searched after every -I) / cpu-limit / mem-limit. Lookup ./madc.ini -> $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/madc/madc.ini -> <sysconfdir>/madc.ini, FIRST EXISTING FILE WINS OUTRIGHT (never merged — a merged chain makes 'why is this setting on?' unanswerable); relative paths resolve against the config FILE's directory; ~/ expands. STRICT parser: unknown key / foreign section / missing '=' / empty value / non-numeric limit = hard error naming file:line + the accepted keys (mem-limit = 8G says so instead of arming an 8 MB guard). New --config=<file> (the whole search, and it MUST load) and --no-config (the two together refuse). The reader is SCHEMA-BLIND SUBSTRATE (madc::cfg::config_file, include/madc_config_file.h): it owns the format, each consumer registers its own keys — the same split madcdis/snapshot.h makes as a CONTENT-blind container — so madcdat and madcdis-based tools reuse it instead of copying a parser; header deliberately UNINSTALLED so a first-draft interface is not frozen into shipped headers. libmadc never reads a config file (a file that can redirect where the compiler loads frozen state from is an attack surface for a sandboxed host); arm 5 rides the enable_external_forest gate with the sidecar/env arms; configure --disable-config-file removes madc's LOOKUP. Batched in: the installed madcdis/snapshot.h now compiles downstream (madc_pch.h, needed by its public signatures, was never installed) and docs/build.md — which still documented asmjit as a build requirement — was rewritten. live_handoff: SESSION 2026-07-26 #10: MACH-O AXIS B STEP 4 COMPLETE + RELEASED v0.52.0 (develop; master stays v0.48.0) — the darwin `.o` lane is REAL. AXIS B IS DONE. WHAT: `madc -c` for a Mach-O target wrote an ELF ET_REL until now — a DOCUMENTED interim ("the `-c` artifacts are ELF-container dev vehicles"), not a hidden defect: madc's own reader consumed them, no Apple tool could. MIR_object_emit on an Apple target now assembles a real MH_OBJECT and MIR_object_read reads one back, so every `.o` lane madc has on ELF works on darwin: `-c` then link, the two-TU merge, `-r` (two `.o` -> one). THE WRITER (mir-macho.c): one unnamed LC_SEGMENT_64 over the SAME section names the executable writer uses (__TEXT,__text / __DATA,__data / __DATA,__bss zerofill LAST / __DATA_CONST,__mir_addrpool / __DATA_CONST,__mod_init_func) so a link by ld64 and a link by MIR's own emitter place things identically; real LC_SYMTAB + LC_DYSYMTAB (locals, then extdefs, then undefs — the DYSYMTAB ranges ARE index ranges, so the grouping is the contract); per-section relocation_info arrays. EVERY relocation is r_extern=1 against a symtab entry: the ELF section symbols relocations target become `ltmp_*' LOCAL LABELS at their section starts (clang's ltmp0 model), so the writer never needs the non-extern form where the field would carry a fake-address-space target instead of a plain addend. ADDENDS, one rule per form (all three verified against a clang-18 .o): UNSIGNED folds the addend into the slot bytes (Mach-O relocations have no addend field); SIGNED stores A + 4 because ld64 resolves S + A' - (P + 4) where ELF resolves S + A - P; the aarch64 instruction-field pairs carry theirs in an ARM64_RELOC_ADDEND entry emitted IMMEDIATELY BEFORE its partner (ld64 applies it to the entry that follows). MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS deliberately NOT set: MIR's pool references address section-relative offsets, so one-atom-per-section is the model the capture already assumes, and with subsections on ld64 rejects an addend reaching past the target symbol's atom. THE READER — ONE MERGE, TWO FRONTS: MIR_object_read now works off a format-neutral input view (objin_t: section bodies + alignments, symbols, relocations, debug) filled by objin_from_elf or objin_from_macho, compile-time exclusive since one target per compiled stack. That was the whole point: a Mach-O copy of the symbol-unification + rebasing logic would have been a parallel implementation of one concern. The conversion was mechanical because the merge already worked off a base[] array and a symbol map — only the accessors moved; the ELF arithmetic is untouched. FAKE ADDRESSES: an MH_OBJECT's section `addr' fields are a linear layout from 0, and the writer sets addr = file offset - segment start (clang's rule) so the vm span can never come out under the file span — the first cut computed them independently and llvm-otool rejected the file ("filesize greater than vmsize"). The reader inverts it: n_value - section addr = the section-relative value the builder wants. MIR_object_load REFUSES LOUDLY on an Apple build instead of mis-parsing: its mapper is ELF-shaped AND mapping text would need MAP_JIT + pthread_jit_write_protect_np on Apple Silicon (only mir-code-alloc-default.c does that), so the lane could not work there regardless of container — that is task #24, with a hardware RUN leg. The lane was never on a gate, which is why a refusal beats half a lane. MADC SIDE: `-g` on a Mach-O target now says so ONCE at the layer the user typed it (neither writer emits __DWARF; the old behavior was the executable writer silently DROPPING an attached debug builder while the new .o writer refuses one outright — the notice keeps the layers honest and consistent). GATE: scripts/macho_obj_gate.sh + `make -C src machogate` — 30 assertions, 15 per arch (arm64 + x86_64), over TWO INDEPENDENT AUTHORITIES: (a) ld64.lld-18 + the macOS SDK links the object, including a MIXED link where a clang-18 TU calls into the madc-compiled one, with pool slots resolving inside __text and __bss and the import slot becoming a real dyld bind; (b) madc's own read-back — `-c` then link disassembles IDENTICALLY to the direct `-o` emit, pool contents included (full-file cmp differs only in the code-signature identifier, which is the output basename). The make target rebuilds BOTH cross madcs first so the gate can never validate a stale binary; it is NOT in fulltest, where its cross-madc / llvm-18 / SDK prerequisites would make it silently skip. THE ROUND-TRIP LEG EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY — it caught a real read-back bug every structural check passed over: Mach-O has ONE ARM64_RELOC_PAGEOFF12 where ELF has LDST64_LO12 and ADD_LO12, so the reader recovers the kind from the instruction's opcode, and the first mask dropped bit 31 (sf) — every `add Xd, Xn, #imm12' read back as a scaled load, immediate #0x1 where the direct emit had #0x8. Structurally valid, silently wrong arithmetic. LESSON TO KEEP: for a format round trip, assert EQUIVALENCE against the path that does not round-trip, not just "the linker accepted it". TRAP FOUND IN THE GATE ITSELF: `llvm-otool -s` dumps section bytes as 4-byte WORDS on arm64 and single BYTES on x86-64 — a byte-only parser silently finds zero slots and the assertion fails on one arch only. VALIDATION OF RECORD: macho_obj_gate 30/30 both arches; Linux fulltest 756/0/0/9, `--exe` 740/0, `--obj` 740/0, packed arbiter 756/0/0/9 (release pack 240 units + ledger) (the ELF `.o` lane itself, since the merge refactor is a shared path); no new warnings either build. Running an emitted Mach-O binary stays the owner's Mac, as in every darwin slice. NEXT: task #23 — `-static-libmadc` in the `.o` link lane (the S5 stated boundary; the fork prerequisite is now in place). KEY FINDING FOR IT: MIR_gen_get_object(ctx) already returns the capture's MIR_object_t (cir_register_tu_init uses it), so no serialize/reparse round trip is needed — set up a context in object mode, pull the ledger, MIR_link, then MIR_object_read each input `.o` INTO that same capture and emit. What still needs designing is the cover-analysis INPUT: today cir_ledger_pull decides what to merge from a compile context's imports, while that lane's imports are the merged builder's UNDEF list (MIR_object_undef_name). NOTE forest_ledger_gate.sh leg 9 currently ASSERTS the refusal — flip it when the lane lands. THEN task #24 (Apple in-process `.o` loader: objin view + MAP_JIT, hardware RUN leg) and the P2 darwin C++ lane (C-lane c++/v1 order, libc++ parse burn-down, libc++ STD-ABI mangled-direct). SMALLER: DK_FPTR arena kind (darwin sig_t), __builtin_va_list as char* on arm64-darwin, prelude growth (sockets), task #22 (compression vocabulary into the madcdis substrate). NEEDS OWNER HARDWARE: every darwin RUN leg (S5's ledger run, and now any .o-lane image). DEFERRED: darwin dylib packaging shape, Windows/PE, the re-signer for already-signed Mach-O. STANDING: QNAP never builds/tests (container ssh -p 2299 dev@localhost does ALL; payloads need an explicit cd /workspace/madc); git commit -F; NEVER git add -A (owner WIP __c-tests-temp.*); cap every test run; one heavy container job (detached nohup + rc-file Monitor — rm the rc file first); CLI flags BEFORE inputs; A QUESTION IS NEVER A DIRECTIVE; the macOS SDK is NEVER committed or synced (container /workspace/sdk/MacOSX.sdk; MACOS_SDK overrides the gate's path); configure is GENERATED/untracked (autoconf in the container AFTER the last sync); scope test runs by BLAST RADIUS and give a GROUP one battery. REHYDRATE: scripts/resume.sh -> this live_handoff -> docs/plans/2026-07-25-macho-arm64-plan.md ("Axis B step 4" section: decisions D1-D9, the gate legs, what this unblocks) -> task #23.

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.

Embedded <iostream> output remains partially staged: cout/cerr/clog still use header-defined stdio-backed ostream bodies. Follow-up is to replace that output surface with real libstdc++ declarations/operators, matching the std::cin direction; do not add stdio.h/FILE* stream bridges.
